text:
jessica: FYI, APAC firewall cutover to default-deny is scheduled 2025-04-02 02:00 UTC. Canary showed node-provisioner POSTs to vault-proxy are being dropped. New GPU nodes fail to decrypt bootstrap secrets.
omar: Which endpoint is impacted exactly?
vikram: POST /v1/session/grant on vault-proxy.apac.internal -> 403 from fw during canary. Connection established but blocked by L7 policy.
ops-bot: [schedule] apac-fw-default-deny -> 02:00 UTC. Noted by @jessica.
jessica: Error log: "access denied: iam condition mismatch". The provisioning path needs kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt scoped to the node role.
tia: Security preference is no blanket KMS grants. We should avoid expanding KMS wide. Short-lived allowlist or a private endpoint exception are preferable.
security-bot: POLICY NOTE: Any temp grant that permits kms:GenerateDataKey must be recorded with tag audit:keystore=true and routed to audit-relay for 72h retention.
omar: Two immediate options: 1) add a scoped fw allow for vault-proxy IPs for the rollout window; 2) create short-lived IAM delegation for the provisioner with a forced audit tag and TTL.
vikram: Option 1 is fastest to get nodes online. Ops can flip an IP allow at 01:45 UTC and revert at 05:00 UTC. Risk: warm-pool churn may extend attempts beyond that window.
jessica: Cost risk if bootstrap loops: last incident burned ~95 GPU-hours -> ~2.3k/day. Also disrupts scheduled rollouts in APAC.
tia: Option 2 is cleaner for compliance but requires infra-scripts change to emit audit events and CloudTrail annotation. Who will build that?
omar: Platform + Security pair. I can prototype attach-detach with TTL=900s. Example draft:```bash
# prototype attach
./infra-scripts/temp-grant.sh --role provisioner --policy provision-kms.json --ttl 900 --tag "audit:keystore=true"
```
vikram: We'll need an automated SIEM push right after grant. Security: can you accept a 5 min window to forward events?
security-bot: Acceptable if the script calls /audit-relay API and receives 2xx before issuing grant. All runs must create an incident (#sec-audit) and include RFC reference.
jessica: Proposed plan: short IP allowlist for vault-proxy for 4h as immediate unblock. Parallel work: land temp-delegation script (TTL=15m) with audit-relay integration by EOD. After validation, revert allowlist.
tia: Approve with caveat: every delegation must include the audit header and SIEM payload within 3m. Also require automated revoke on TTL expiry.
omar: I'll own allowlist flip and cron rollback (will post script & IPs 45m prior).
vikram: I'll open PR for infra-scripts with the audit-relay hook. Requesting security review @tia.
ops-bot: [alert created] apac-gpu-bootstrap-failures threshold=5/10m by omar.
jessica: Please file a short_change RFC in #infra-rfcs with the rule IDs. Security requires RFC before 01:00 UTC.
omar: RFC filed: https://rfc.internal/17652-apac-provision-exception (link). PR draft: https://git.internal/infra-scripts/pulls/228 (will update).
tia: I'll review the PR once CI passes. Also add a dashboard: live boot success rate and KMS grant events.
jessica: Quick checklist for rollout: 1) ops flip allowlist 01:45; 2) platform land delegation script + SIEM handshake; 3) enable alert + dashboards; 4) revert allowlist after stable.
omar: Script snippet I'll run:```bash
# flip allowlist
./ops/flip-fw-rule.sh --zone apac --allow 10.101.12.23,10.101.12.24 --expires "2025-04-02T05:00:00Z"
# rollback via cron if not reverted
/bin/at 05:05 <<'EOF'
./ops/flip-fw-rule.sh --zone apac --remove 10.101.12.23,10.101.12.24
EOF
```
vikram: Note: ensure the allowlist rule is tagged short_change=true in firewall audit logs. Security checks that tag.
security-bot: Reminder: any firewall change must annotate RFC id and short_change tag. Non-compliant changes will be auto-rolled by policy.
jessica: Thanks team. I'll coordinate cutover window and post final timeline. Follow-ups: PR link, RFC link, allowlist script in thread.
